title: Business Requirements Document — Hospital Patient Portal

sections.title: 1. Executive Summary & Strategic Rationale
sections.body: The Hospital Patient Portal is a proposed digital platform designed to facilitate secure communication and information exchange between hospital staff and patients. The strategic rationale for this system is to improve patient engagement, streamline administrative workflows, and ensure secure handling of Protected Health Information (PHI). As the source document excerpt is unavailable, the specific strategic drivers, current operational pain points, and long-term digital transformation goals are currently undefined and require stakeholder input to establish the foundational business case.

sections.title: 2. Business Objectives & Success Metrics
sections.body: The primary business objectives for the Hospital Patient Portal are to enhance patient experience, reduce administrative burden on hospital staff, and ensure strict compliance with healthcare data privacy regulations. However, specific, measurable success metrics (e.g., patient adoption rates, reduction in call center volume, or time-to-resolution for patient inquiries) are not defined in the available source material. Defining these KPIs is an open item requiring stakeholder alignment.

sections.title: 3. Scope & Operational Boundaries (In/Out of Scope)
sections.body: The operational scope of the Hospital Patient Portal is expected to encompass secure patient authentication, viewing of medical records, appointment scheduling, and secure messaging with healthcare providers. The exact boundaries of the system, including specific modules to be included (In-Scope) and explicitly excluded (Out-of-Scope, such as billing integration or third-party wearable device data ingestion), are not detailed in the provided source. Clarifying these operational boundaries is a critical open item for the project initiation phase.

sections.title: 4. Key Stakeholders & Governance Personas
sections.body: Key stakeholders for the Hospital Patient Portal typically include hospital administration, IT security officers, clinical staff (doctors, nurses), and the end-users (patients). Specific governance personas, their respective roles, and their approval authorities are not identified in the source material. Identifying the primary decision-makers and the governance structure for requirement changes is an open item requiring stakeholder input.

sections.title: 5. Business Requirements Specification Matrix
table: The system must provide a secure method for patients to log in and verify their identity.
Open item: Specific authentication protocols (e.g., MFA) and success criteria require stakeholder definition.
The system must protect Protected Health Information in accordance with applicable healthcare regulations.
Open item: Specific data handling and access control criteria require stakeholder definition.
Patients must be able to view their relevant medical records securely.
Open item: Scope of records (e.g., lab results, discharge summaries) and access criteria require stakeholder definition.

sections.title: 6. Assumptions & Operational Constraints
sections.body: Assumptions regarding the technical infrastructure, patient digital literacy, and integration with existing hospital systems (e.g., Electronic Health Records) are not stated in the source document. Operational constraints, such as budget limitations, timeline expectations, or specific hardware requirements for patient access, are currently undefined. Documenting these assumptions and constraints is an open item requiring stakeholder input.

sections.title: 7. Risk & Compliance Baseline
sections.body: The Hospital Patient Portal must adhere to strict healthcare compliance frameworks, including HIPAA and GDPR (if applicable to EU patients), as well as data interchange standards like HL7 FHIR and DICOM. The compliance baseline mandates PHI encryption at rest using AES-256, immutability of audit trails, and high availability standards with a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of less than 1 hour and a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of less than 5 minutes. Specific risk factors, mitigation strategies, and compliance verification procedures are not detailed in the source material and require further stakeholder analysis.
